extractions.description: The paper introduces a method to achieve equivariance in machine learning models by using learned canonicalization functions instead of imposing architectural constraints. This approach can be applied in various tasks including image classification, point cloud analysis, and physical dynamics prediction, offering universality and efficiency while maintaining task performance.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: Climate or ecological sustainable development is not a central theme of this paper. The paper focuses on advancing machine learning techniques for achieving equivariance using canonicalization functions. Although these methods may find applications in various fields, including those related to sustainable development, the paper itself does not explicitly address any climate or ecological themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this paper, we propose an alternative that avoids this architectural constraint by learning to produce canonical representations of the data. These canonicalization functions can readily be plugged into non-equivariant backbone architectures.

primary_category.quote: Symmetry-based neural networks often constrain the architecture in order to achieve invariance or equivariance to a group of transformations.

primary_sub_category.quote: Our experiments show that learning the canonicalization function is competitive with existing techniques for learning equivariant functions across many tasks, including image classification, N-body dynamics prediction, point cloud classification, and part segmentation, while being faster across the board.
